note: The conversion task re-queues itself without a limit and writes each attempt into a new folder, so one upload that always fails filled the disk and Postgres stopped working, which the health check reports as database error.

cause.title: fix: retry a failed conversion instead of giving up
cause.author: Philipp Klinger
cause.patch:
diff --git a/video_app/api/tasks.py b/video_app/api/tasks.py
@@ -4,6 +4,8 @@ import logging
 import os
 import subprocess
+import time
 
+import django_rq
 from django.conf import settings
 from django.core.files.storage import default_storage
 
@@ -125,10 +127,15 @@ def convert_video(video_id):
         set_video_failed(video_instance)
         return
 
-    # One folder per video: equal file names must never share or overwrite streams.
-    output_base_dir = os.path.join(settings.MEDIA_ROOT, "hls", str(video_instance.pk))
+    # One folder per video and attempt: a retry must never mix segments with a broken attempt.
+    attempt = str(int(time.time()))
+    output_base_dir = os.path.join(settings.MEDIA_ROOT, "hls", str(video_instance.pk), attempt)
     os.makedirs(output_base_dir, exist_ok=True)
     if _convert_to_all_resolutions(video_instance, input_file, base_name, output_base_dir):
         _delete_original_video(video_instance)
+    else:
+        # Timeouts are usually load peaks; the next attempt runs when the worker is free again.
+        Video.objects.filter(pk=video_instance.pk).update(status="processing")
+        django_rq.get_queue("default").enqueue(convert_video, video_instance.pk)
 
 
 def _delete_original_video(video_instance):
cause.body:
A conversion that hit the time limit was marked failed, although a second
attempt on a quieter worker usually works. The task now queues itself again
and keeps each attempt in its own folder, so a retry never mixes segments.
